reconstructed_theorem_text: Let Omega be a measurable space and E a compact second-countable topological space with its Borel measurable structure. Let P be a probability measure on Omega; X:[0,infinity) x Omega -> E jointly measurable with continuous paths for P-almost every omega; g:E->R continuous; and A:[0,infinity) x E->R jointly continuous. Suppose that for every t>=0 there exists a real random variable Z_t, integrable under P and with integral zero, such that for P-almost every omega, g(X(t,omega))-g(X(0,omega))=integral_{v=0}^{t} A(v^+,X(v^+,omega)) dv+Z_t(omega), where v^+=max(v,0) is regarded as NNReal. The exceptional set and Z_t may depend on t. Then for every s>=0 the real function F(r)=integral g(X(r^+,omega)) dP(omega) has derivative within [0,infinity) at s equal to integral A(s,X(s,omega)) dP(omega). This is a right derivative at s=0 and an ordinary derivative at positive s, expressed uniformly as HasDerivWithinAt on the nonnegative half-line.
objects: Omega,E,P,X,g,A, per-time integrable zero-mean Z_t, expectation function F, derivative time s.
domains: E compact and second-countable with Borel measurable space; no Hausdorff or metric hypothesis is explicitly present. Time for X,A is NNReal; derivative variable is real.
quantifiers: For all Omega,E,P,X,g,A satisfying the assumptions, including for every t there exists Z_t with an a.e. balance, for every s>=0 the within-derivative assertion follows.
assumptions: P probability; X jointly measurable and a.e. globally continuous paths; g continuous; A jointly continuous; for each t exists integrable mean-zero Z_t giving the stated balance a.e.
conclusion: Derivative of E_P[g(X_s)] within [0,infinity) equals E_P[A(s,X_s)] for every s>=0.
scopes: Path continuity has a single full-measure event for all nonnegative time; balance a.e. events may vary with t; derivative holds at every deterministic s, no a.e.-in-time restriction. F is extended to negative real arguments through r^+.
constant_dependencies: Z_t may depend on t and the supplied process/data; no common random variable or martingale property is asserted. Derivative is determined by A,X,P,s.
